analysis_notes.notes:
Torah LM2 #22 has no entries whatsoever in torahData.js (reference 1022 is absent from the dataset entirely). The source text (torah_22.txt) is four sentences long and teaches a single principle: that true humility (הַכְנָעָה) is easily misunderstood, because naive self-abasement without דַּעַת merely drops a person into מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת (small-mindedness), and is therefore equivalent to חֲנֻפָּה (flattery), not genuine humility. Only Moses, who possessed consummate דַּעַת, could practice true humility.

Gap analysis — bechina language survey:
The source text does not use any explicit bechina-equation language of the form 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y'. The nearest structural points are:
1. הַכְנָעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּרָאוּי = חֲנֻפָּה — The Rabbis of the Talmud (Sotah 41b) label improper humility as flattery. This is a Talmudic legal-ethical categorization cited by Rebbe Nachman, not a bechina equation authored by the Rebbe himself. It does not establish a shared-nature identity between the two concepts in the Rebbe Nachman framework.
2. הַכְנָעָה / מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת — The text states that naive humility causes entry into מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת. This is an eitza (causal) relationship, not a bechina (shared-nature) identity.
3. הַכְנָעָה / דַּעַת — The text states that true humility requires דַּעַת. This is a prerequisite/eitza relationship.

Conclusion: No bechina (parallel-nature) equations are present in the text. No missing nodes are flagged. No orphaned dataset nodes exist (the dataset is empty for this Torah). No additions are proposed.
